rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice for forming or coming up with an idea.

example.english: I finally managed to conceive a good solution.
example.traditional: 我終於諗出嚟一個好方法。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 nam2 ceot1 lai4 jat1 go3 hou2 fong1 faat3

rows.note: Use this specifically for conceiving or imagining something in the mind rather than developing a concrete idea.

example.english: I really can't conceive of him running that fast.
example.traditional: 我真係想像唔到佢可以跑咁快。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 soeng2 zoeng6 m4 dou2 keoi5 ho2 ji5 paau2 gam3 faai3

rows.note: Use this colloquially when the context makes clear that someone has become pregnant.

example.english: My wife is pregnant, and we finally managed to conceive a child.
example.traditional: 我老婆有咗，成家人都好開心。
example.jyutping: ngo5 lou5 po4 jau5 zo2 seng4 gaa1 jan4 dou1 hou2 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use this when stating explicitly and neutrally that someone has become pregnant, rather than using the colloquial 有咗.

example.english: The doctor said she was three months pregnant, so they had managed to conceive three months ago.
example.traditional: 醫生話佢已經懷孕三個月。
example.jyutping: ji1 saang1 waa6 keoi5 ji5 ging1 waai4 jan6 saam1 go3 jyut6
